AWS.description: Amazon Web Services address ranges per service, across all regions. AMAZON and EC2 are rentable space. These ranges also host other customers' workloads, so allowing them lets anything running there through.

Cloudflare.description: Cloudflare's edge network ranges. These ranges also host other customers' workloads, so allowing them lets anything running there through.

GitHub.description: GitHub's address ranges per service, from the GitHub meta API.

Google.description: Google's own front ends: Gmail, Drive, Meet and the other Workspace apps, kept apart from Google Cloud.

Google Cloud.description: Google Cloud customer and service ranges, all regions. These ranges also host other customers' workloads, so allowing them lets anything running there through.

Microsoft 365 China (21Vianet).description: Microsoft sorts these endpoints into three categories: Optimize, Allow and Default. Most sites want All categories, which combines the three.

Microsoft 365 US Gov DoD.description: Microsoft sorts these endpoints into three categories: Optimize, Allow and Default. Most sites want All categories, which combines the three.

Microsoft 365 US Gov GCC High.description: Microsoft sorts these endpoints into three categories: Optimize, Allow and Default. Most sites want All categories, which combines the three.

Microsoft 365 Worldwide.description: Microsoft sorts these endpoints into three categories: Optimize, Allow and Default. Most sites want All categories, which combines the three.

Microsoft Azure.description: Azure service tags, one list per service across all regions. AzureCloud is all of Azure's public space. These ranges also host other customers' workloads, so allowing them lets anything running there through.
